newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Eurotunnel share group attacks plan.
newsitem.headline: French Eurotunnel share group attacks plan.

text.p: Adacte, a French group representing Eurotunnel SA /Plc shareholders, attacked on Wednesday a debt restructuring plan agreed between the company and bankers.

The Association de Defense des Actionnaires d'Eurotunnel said in a statement an agreement at the last minute after 12 months of talks meant the firm had incurred five billion francs of interest and blamed the banks for holding out so long.

It said that if the company had gone into insolvency protection, imposed by the commercial court, and carried on operating through a "plan of continuation" a better financial restructuring would have been acheived than the present.

The plan agreed on Tuesday "could only be inferior to a plan of continuation - similar to a legal administration in English insolvency - which would have allowed Eurotunnel to repay principal without interest payment, it said.
The agreement with the banks meant there will be no search for those responsible for Eurotunnel's problems, it said.
Adacte said it has appointed an accountant, Eric Habib, who is a specialist in corporate recoveries, to analyse the agreement and to compare it with a plan of continuation.
Any debt restructuring requires a qualified majority of shareholders.

Earlier, another grouping, the Eurotunnel Shareholders Association, said it was asking for a meeting with Eurotunnel management in the next few days once the details of the agreement were known, so it could decide its position.
The association said it has gathered 32 percent of voting rights, which was near a blocking minority.
